chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Ship's officers befriend Crawford on the way to Europe
summary: Crawford recalls Polish ship officers gathering around him and asking about America.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, all I remember is for some reason most all people were just crazy about me. I don't know whether it was my personality. Wasn't my drumming. And so even on the boat, M. S. [Polish boat Pretori] the officers would gather around me --
You say the -- even the officers on the ship would like --

They all liked me for some reason. I'd find myself -- officers on the deck, in my stateroom, just talking, just general conversations. They wanted to know about America. I want -- well, you know, like places to go and visit and that -- of course, I don't want [them that] to become agents, you know, like CIA or FBI or anything like that. I don't know anything about that stuff, although I know they're in your mail, listening to your phone calls. Well, let them listen.

One thing I'm proud to say, I never was on dope.
